decisions.reason: Adding site header navigation does not necessarily replace the existing shared visual treatment or informational-page header logo; the source does not specify a change to those treatments.
A header menu can coexist with footer links, and the source does not remove or revise the footer's content or page-link strategy.
The source decision concerns navigation for the public website, not the separate Console-shell and application navigation panels.
The same message separately updates the Console's look and layout, but the website header-menu decision does not alter the Console shell styling requirement.
The source does not state that the new website header menu changes the sign-in page's branding, background, logo, footer, or informational-page treatment.
Although the new menu may eventually require responsive design, the source establishes no responsive rule, breakpoint, or behavior change.
The agent diagram is separately introduced by another clause of the same message; adding navigation to its associated page does not change the diagram requirement.
The platform diagram is separately introduced by another clause of the same message; the header-menu change does not alter its placement, source artifact, or deliverable.
The source does not connect the new header navigation to the provisioning wizard or revise its background, logo, footer, or styling-rework requirements.
Adding a header menu does not change the established implementation stack or handoff objective, and no new handoff obligation is stated.
The header navigation is an independent page-chrome behavior and does not revise the landing page's recorded theme, typography, colors, approval, or spacing.
The source provides no new token values, token categories, font assets, dimensions, or component-state specifications.
